intro: Picture a town without streets. You are at Çatalhöyük, a mound in Konya province dating to 7400 BC, and one of the world's earliest urban settlements.
history: Some 8,000 people once lived here, and they entered their houses through the roof. Their wall paintings and mother-goddess figurines are landmarks of prehistoric art.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the North excavation shelter and the Experimental house. Look for the wall paintings, and then head on to the South mound.
facts: Did you know? This 9,000-year-old settlement has no streets. Houses were built wall to wall and entered by ladder through the roof, so the rooftops were the street. The dead were buried beneath the floors of the houses, under the platforms where the family slept. And one wall painting shows a settlement plan from above, with an erupting volcano behind it. It is considered by some the world's oldest known map, and the oldest known depiction of a volcano.
outro: This brings our journey through Çatalhöyük to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
